answer: At its kernel, a bond-and-slash design makes sybils expensive: every agent must lock real stake before it can act, and any provable misbehavior slashes that bond. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then means funding a thousand bonds, opening a canyon-wide gap between forgery cost and expected reward. Honest agents earn rewards that vest slowly, composed line by line like a sonnet, while attackers simply watch their locked capital burn.
